title: Nothing in the Sky Takes a Week. So Why 7 Days?
lines: Why does a week have {7 days~seven days}?
Almost everything on your calendar comes from the sky. | Except the week.
A day, one {spin/~spin} of the Earth.
{A month about/~A month, about} one lunar cycle.
A year, one {trip/~trip} around the Sun.
But nothing up {there/~there} takes a week.
Historians trace the number to Babylon, | and its {7~seven} moving lights.
The Sun, the Moon, | and {5~five} planets.
Rome gave each {day/~day} to one of them.
Saturday is Saturn's day. | Sunday, the Sun's. | Monday, the Moon's.
The Soviets {tried/~tried} {5-~five-} and {6-day~six-day} weeks. | By {1940~nineteen forty}, {7~seven} was back.
Under the Soviet {5-day week,~five-day week,} did everyone get the same day off? | Yes, one shared day off, | or no, it rotated? | Tell me in the comments.

preroll.line: In {1793,~seventeen ninety-three,} France tried to replace the week with {10 days.~ten days.}
